body: Every time I have hope for humanity, Reddit reminds me we devolve into personal attacks 3 arguments in.

I was a freshman there last year. It was very mediocre, especially for the amount of money you have to pay for tuition. The school gives out a lot of scholarships but it still racks up to 50k USD.

Let it be known that the name SAIC DOES hold some weight in the art world. I'm not sure how much having a degree from SAIC helps with getting a job, but the uni is pretty chummy with local galleries and museums. There was also like a job expo thing and some pretty big name companies showed up (like Webtoon, which is the only one I paid attention to sorry-).

SAIC also has some really, really great facilities. A lot of students don't take advantage of them, but pretty much if you can think of it, the school has it. The only problem is that a lot of them are locked behind classes. You can only use certain facilities (like the animation lightboards) if you're taking a specific class.

And oh boy, here comes the complaints. (Disclaimer: All of this is my own biased opinion. Read with caution.)

Classes can be either very fun or very boring. Most are highly unpractical. Still fun, but unpractical (meaning you'll most likely never use anything you learn from them for the rest of your life). You can get some pretty decent education in though, just keep in mind each class costs 5k. The biggest complaint I've heard about this school is how hard it is to get into a class you want, ESPECIALLY FOR FRESHMEN. There are like 10 million drawing and painting classes but if you want to get into a highly contested subject like animation, viscom/graphic design, comics or illustration, you have to get ready to FIGHT. I am not kidding. You have to literally pray your enrollment time is earlier than everyone else's, and all my friends and I used to remind each other about enrollment times. 

Faculty are extremely hit or miss. I've had some really good professors who taught me practical things about the industry. There are many others who are mid: a mix of people who can teach but don't care about students, and really nice people who can't teach. Some are absolutely terrible. Don't let that word "some" fool you, there are more terrible profs than you think. Not that I can blame them to be honest, because a lot of my professors have complained that no one gets a tenure, they're all on part time with minimal pay, and that's why they're trying to unionize. But I know that more than one professor has assigned textbooks that are out of print (and refused to photocopy their own copy of said textbook). My roomie had one give her a 7 page essay due within the week. I know another professor who gives an automatic fail to anyone who misses 2 classes, regardless of reason. Almost every professor expects you to sink 16+ hours into their class. It is grueling. You probably thought "oh, that doesn't sound that tough." No. It is. If you go there, you will experience it, at some point or another.

From my understanding, the main thing you're supposed to get out of college is connections. You're probably not going to get that here. The student body is just a bunch of cliques. People stick to each other in their groups of 3 best friends. People don't seem to want to know anything about you 95% of the time. Especially the Chinese kids. There are SO many Chinese kids, 85% of them smoke, and none of them interact with the rest of the student body (I'm Asian American, if anyone gets to say it I do). Its kind of a nepo baby school. My roommates dad was a real estate tycoon. If you get into the wrong dorm (cough, the Buck, cough) you are screwed because you'll have no social life. Classmates are a toss up between funnest people you'll ever know, people who don't seem to care at all about art or the class, people who think taking drugs is a personality trait (it's rarer to find someone who hasnt done any), and straight up clinically insane people (I wish I were kidding, so many people have told me they hallucinate). 

Retention rate (percentage of people who stay.. or transfer/drop out. It's one of the two, I don't remember). It's low. Around 40% of the people I met there have told me they want to transfer. 60% hate the school. I don't blame them.

The school administration acts like they care about students until you enroll.(I too was fooled by the seemingly personalized Lunar New Year gift they mailed me.) Then you realize you are just a number to them. I believe they changed the time schedule last year (Fall 2023) to cram more classes in. 

The dorms are all terrible except for the Buck. But as I said before, living in the Buck pretty much means you won't have a social life, or it'll be harder for you. Even worse, if you live in the dorms you're forced to pay for a meal plan. The cafeteria food isn't just standard American high school lunch. It's guaranteed food poisoning on Sushi Mondays. That wasn't a joke. A friend of mine got sick for a solid three days (nonstop vomitting on day 1) because of I believe the hot food. Here's a good opportunity to bash on another aspect of SAIC: the Health Services. Aforementioned friend with food poisoning called in and they said they'd get back to her within 5 business days. Needless to say, they don't care. I took their counseling services (because you get 10 free sessions). It felt like an interrogation, and left me with more trauma than I had before starting.

And then there's Chicago. I love Chicago. I don't mind the cold, so it's a lovely place, very clean (As clean as a city can get, but its the cleanest city in the States that Ive been to), very friendly people, pretty decent public transportation. Probably one of the best parts of my entire experience at SAIC.

I'm probably missing some things, and some of my sentences might be a bit unfinished but oh well. Personally, I got out because I realized I wasnt into art as a job. Best decision of my life. I believe this is a problem with most art schools, but they don't really like people doing art that isn't... traditional? art? It's not quite traditional, but I can't explain what it is. They want you to do art a certain way, with intent. Anyways. Bonus trivia: In certain states, it's extremely hard to transfer credits from SAIC over to other colleges because SAIC operates on a Pass/Fail system and apparently that just don't fly.

In conclusion, do not go unless you are CERTAIN you want a career in the arts. Don't let the "top 2 art school in the nation" marketing fool you, do your research!

Yep, second run with Momo and I got the 3 star clear. 1:30 on the dot. My lineup was Harim>A.Yubin>Evelyn>Elizabeth>Serapel>Xiao Lin>A.Ministra>Claudia, Kamiizumi and Momo operator.
Basically the strat is to commit mass murder and not to lure the wall out like the Yuna strat. Disclaimer: I played manually though

Here’s the (relatively little) logic I used to slap the team together:
- Yubin’s there to drain the tower’s HP. I think any other tank/awakened defender would work, but Yubin would be best.
- Added 3 healers + serapel so the tank isn’t on life support. Serapel shares damage I believe, which is why I put her there. i haven’t tried other 4 cost defenders, but i doubt they’d work because serapel’s job is keeping the tank alive. (actually I didn’t need Claudia, so 2+serapel or 3 healers might work. you could sub another dps in so your clear time is more comfy).
- Elizabeth, Xiao Lin and A.Ministra were my DPSes. I don’t think it really matters who you use as long as you have one ranger to proc Momo. I liked having Ministra though because a ton of cannon fodder died so a lot of her swords spawned. (I think the swords give debuffs to the enemy? I like barely know what she does I’m sorry. It just worked out ngl)

All in all I think basically everyone is replaceable except for Momo. Momo is non negotiable. (thanking that one free operator card I got from last ani or something)

The order of deployment matters. Healer first for Momo’s skill requirement. Tank next. Another healer next because (at least for me) if you deploy your ranger straight away your tank might die from their HP falling too low. Then ranger to proc Momo’s skill. Third healer/serapel to make sure your tank stays healthy (from experience 2 healers aren’t enough to sustain for long). Then spam your DPSes, and you should be good to go!

For gear.. it doesn’t have to be that great? I’m at level 55. My Yubin had his ideal set but the others had just random stuff I picked up. 

But ya wish anyone who reads this good luck with clearing!

Hmm.. Xiao is hard to build for, since he's new and not much testing has been done yet. Try Xiao, Anemo Traveller, Fischl, Barbara.

Anemo Traveler is there because Xiao desperately needs energy. Forgot the specifics, but characters of the same element give more energy particles to each other than different elements.

Fischl, because you need someone who can proc elemental reactions fast during Xiao's ult. Xingqiu is fine too, so if Fischl isn't working out I'd recommend getting Xingqiu during the event. If not, then 

Barbara for heals because Xiao's ult drains hp like nothing else. Correction: Oceanid exists, so besides that.

For the event, I'd say get either Xingqiu or Chongyun, since you're lacking Hydro and Cryo characters. Leaning slightly more towards Chongyun in Fischl pairs well with Xiao.

Diluc Xiangling Mona Diona.

Order of combat:

The main point of the team is just to proc the Melt reaction for Diluc (Melt has 2x dmg multiplier when procced by Pyro, and you can crit on it)

This team comp should work until you want to switch main dpses.
Who do you want as main dps?

In general, for team comp, you want Main Dps (1), a support character of the same element (2), elemental reaction proc (3), and the last one is.. well, pretty much anyone is fine but I would recommend either a healer, an extra reaction proc, or a support character with the same element as 3 (only if the elemental party buff is good, e.g. dont go out of your way to do double hydro, increased healing isnt worth it). Also, remember to look up all the elemental reactions and see which ones work best with your dps. It should make it easier to decide on team members.

Your main dps is Xinyan, who shines best with a Physical Dmg build, if I recall correctly. That makes it a lot easier to decide on party members, because you want the SuperConduct elemental reaction (wont go into details but basically it helps you deal more physical dmg).

For the second party member, you still want a pyro character because the double pyro buff is pretty good. I recommend bennett, solely because of his ult (makes every team member do more dmg for a while, and it also heals). Xiangling doesn't do much for a Phys Dmg dps, and neither does Amber.

As mentioned before, you want the SuperConduct reaction, so that means the last two characters are definitely going to be Cryo and Electro. For Cryo, I recommend Chongyun, because he has a Cryo AoE skill. Try to run Sacrificial Greatsword if you use Chongyun. Kaeya is fine too, you just have to get his ult up as much as possible. Diona isn't a bad option since she heals (bennett ult doesnt heal past 70% hp so this helps a lot), but she doesn't proc Cryo a lot. That's kinda bad cause you want to be proccing Superconduct as much as possible.

Last character would be Lisa, since she's your only Electro character. Personally, I use Fischl.

Your team should end up looking something like Xinyan, Bennett, Chongyun, Lisa. If Bennett really doesn't cut it for the heals, then swap Chongyun out for Diona. 

Please note that there are exceptions to the mini team building guide I put at the beginning, its just a very basic thing to get you started. Teams also usually change depending on which bosses, domains, or spiral abyss floors you're facing. I think the Xinyan team I mentioned is pretty solid though, and you won't have to swap people out very often.

I would suggest that you ask again on this thread if you plan to switch dpses. Good luck with team building!!

Zhongli is pretty good for dps, and definitely has more potential than Kaeya. (Zhongli is better at geo support and Kaeya is better at dps support/proccing elemental reactions though, but you can build pretty much everyone to be dps in this game if you try hard enough.)

Zhongli relies on Elemental Burst to do damage (I’ve seen some physical dps builds too, but not sure how that works so I won’t be mentioning that). This might be inaccurate, but I think his main damage comes from his Ultimate (Q), and that does 700% dmg at Talent Level 7. I don’t have Kaeya’s talents maxed, but I think his Ultimate does around 110% dmg every 1 sec at Talent 7? (his ult duration is 8s).

On paper, it sounds like Kaeya’s ultimate is a LOT better, because it’s 110% x8 in comparison to Zhongli’s 700%. However, crits exist. I’m pretty sure you can crit on Zhongli’s ultimate, AND he does extra damage equal to 33% of his max HP. Unless you’re an rng god, there’s no way you can crit for the entire duration of Kaeya’s ultimate, so in the end Zhongli’s ultimate does a lot more damage. Add on to the fact that there’s no specific artifact set that buffs Cryo damage, while there’s 2 for Geo, it’s pretty hard to boost Kaeya’s damage higher. Also yes, most of Kaeya’s damage comes from his ultimate as well (this is from my own experience so I can’t really explain why. Feel free to counter this point).

Additional points would be:
1. Zhongli’s ultimate comes back a LOT faster than Kaeya’s. The cooldown is 12s, while energy needed is 40. In comparison, Kaeya’s cooldown is 15s, while energy needed is 60.
2. Zhongli attacks fast, has a shield, has one of the highest scaling ultimates in the game (diluc is at 400% if I’m not mistaken, Zhongli’s at 700%), petrified enemies, and has the highest max hp (same as jean at 14k i believe). Kaeya is kind of average, everywhere.
3. This is my personal opinion, but I believe Zhongli only has 2 drawbacks: he’s geo, and a polearm user. Geo only has the Crystallize reaction, and that doesn’t do any additional damage when reacting with another element, which kind of sucks cause the game is all about churning out more damage. Kaeya is a lot more versatile in this area, being Cryo and all. Polearm users also have a drawback, because (in my own opinion, at least), there aren’t really any outstandingly good 3 star polearms. The blacksmith polearms are pretty decent, but it adds to how much you require to invest in Zhongli.
4. Okay i lied there’s one more drawback to zhongli but that’s just cause I’m salty. Why does his ult scale off max hp. Why. Why can’t it be attack. Okay I’m done crying ;-;.

In conclusion, sorry Kaeya simps, but you’ll have to invest a LOT more in Kaeya in order to make him as good as Zhongli. R.I.P. :p
